claim: Transition metals, such as zinc, are essential micronutrients in all organisms.
source: Transition metals, such as zinc, are essential micronutrients in all organisms, but also highly toxic in excessive amounts.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about transition metals.

claim: Transition metals are highly toxic in excessive amounts.
source: Transition metals, such as zinc, are essential micronutrients in all organisms, but also highly toxic in excessive amounts.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about transition metal toxicity.

claim: Heavy-metal transporting P-type (PIB) ATPases are crucial for homeostasis.
source: Heavy-metal transporting P-type (PIB) ATPases are crucial for homeostasis, conferring cellular detoxification and redistribution through transport of these ions across cellular membranes.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the manuscript.

claim: No structural information is available for the PIB-4-ATPases.
source: No structural information is available for the PIB-4-ATPases, the subclass with the broadest cargo scope, and hence even their topology remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases have the broadest cargo scope among PIB-ATPases.
source: No structural information is available for the PIB-4-ATPases, the subclass with the broadest cargo scope, and hence even their topology remains elusive.
evidence: This is supported by the discussion of metal specificity in the manuscript and citations.

claim: The topology of PIB-4-ATPases remains elusive.
source: No structural information is available for the PIB-4-ATPases, the subclass with the broadest cargo scope, and hence even their topology remains elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: Structures of sCoaT from Sulfitobacter sp. NAS14-1 were determined.
source: Here, we present structures and complementary functional analyses of an archetypal PIB-4-ATPase, sCoaT from Sulfitobacter sp. NAS14-1.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by crystallographic data.

claim: sCoaT is an archetypal PIB-4-ATPase.
source: Here, we present structures and complementary functional analyses of an archetypal PIB-4-ATPase, sCoaT from Sulfitobacter sp. NAS14-1.
evidence: This is stated in the manuscript and supported by sequence analysis.

claim: The sCoaT structures are devoid of classical heavy-metal-binding domains (HMBDs).
source: The data disclose the architecture, devoid of classical so-called heavy-metal-binding domains (HMBDs), and provide fundamentally new insights into the mechanism and diversity of heavy-metal transporters.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing only 47 residues unmodelled, insufficient for a classical HMBD.

claim: An invariant histidine has a dual role in heavy-metal release and as an internal counter ion.
source: We reveal several novel P-type ATPase features, including a dual role in heavy-metal release and as an internal counter ion of an invariant histidine.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing H657 position and functional assays of H657A mutant.

claim: The turnover of PIB-ATPases is potassium independent.
source: We also establish that the turnover of PIB-ATPases is potassium independent, contrasting to many other P-type ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by potassium titration experiments showing no effect on ATPase activity.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases function as virulence factors in many pathogens.
source: Combined with new inhibitory compounds, our results open up for efforts in for example drug discovery, since PIB-4-ATPases function as virulence factors in many pathogens.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on pathogen virulence.

claim: Malfunctioning of ATP7A causes Menkes disease.
source: Indeed, malfunctioning of the human PIB-members, ATP7A and ATP7B, cause the fatal neurological Menkes disease and Wilson disease (Bull et al., 1993; Vulpe et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Malfunctioning of ATP7B causes Wilson disease.
source: Indeed, malfunctioning of the human PIB-members, ATP7A and ATP7B, cause the fatal neurological Menkes disease and Wilson disease (Bull et al., 1993; Vulpe et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: PIB-ATPases belong to the P-type ATPase superfamily of integral membrane proteins.
source: The PIB-ATPases belong to the P-type ATPase superfamily of integral membrane proteins, which exploit energy from ATP hydrolysis for transport of cargo across cellular membranes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about protein classification.

claim: P-type ATPases exploit energy from ATP hydrolysis for transport of cargo across cellular membranes.
source: The PIB-ATPases belong to the P-type ATPase superfamily of integral membrane proteins, which exploit energy from ATP hydrolysis for transport of cargo across cellular membranes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about P-type ATPase mechanism.

claim: P-type ATPases share an overall mechanism described by the Post-Albers cycle.
source: These proteins share an overall mechanism described by the so-called Post-Albers cycle (Albers et al., 1963; Post and Sen, 1965), as established by decades of structural and functional investigations of primarily Ca2+-, Na+/K+-, and H+-specific P-type ATPases (Toyoshima et al., 2000; Toyoshima and Nomura, 2002; Toyoshima et al., 2004; Olesen et al., 2004; Olesen et al., 2007; Winther et al., 2013; Toyoshima et al., 2013; Morth et al., 2007; Shinoda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by extensive citations to previous research.

claim: The Post-Albers cycle includes four cornerstone states: E1–E1P–E2P–E2.
source: In summary, four cornerstone states, E1–E1P–E2P–E2, provide alternating access and affinity for the transported ions (and counterions, if present).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the P-type ATPase mechanism.

claim: PIB-ATPases are subdivided into groups based on conserved sequence motifs and selectivity towards transported transition metal ions.
source: PIB-ATPases are subdivided into groups based on conserved sequence motifs and the selectivity towards transported transition metal ions (Smith et al., 2014; Argüello, 2003; Zielazinski et al., 2012; Zhitnitsky and Lewinson, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous classification studies.

claim: PIB-4 proteins comprise some of the simplest and shortest proteins within the entire P-type ATPase superfamily.
source: Whereas Cu+- and Zn2+-transporting PIB-1 and PIB-2 ATPases are relatively well characterized, little is known regarding the PIB-4 proteins, which comprise some of the simplest and shortest proteins within the entire P-type ATPase superfamily (Smith et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous analysis.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases are present in plants, archaea, and prokaryotes.
source: They are present in plants, archaea, and prokaryotes, and have been assigned a role as virulence factors in pathogens, as for example the PIB-4-ATPase MtCtpD is required for tuberculosis infections (Sassetti and Rubin, 2003; Joshi et al., 2006), and therefore represent attractive targets for novel antibiotics.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MtCtpD is required for tuberculosis infections.
source: They are present in plants, archaea, and prokaryotes, and have been assigned a role as virulence factors in pathogens, as for example the PIB-4-ATPase MtCtpD is required for tuberculosis infections (Sassetti and Rubin, 2003; Joshi et al., 2006), and therefore represent attractive targets for novel antibiotics.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases are classically referred to as cobalt transporters.
source: The PIB-4-ATPases are classically referred to as cobalt transporters.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical classification of PIB-4-ATPases.

claim: The metal specificity of PIB-4-ATPases remains elusive.
source: However, the metal specificity of the PIB-4-ATPases remains elusive as some members have a confirmed cobalt specificity, while others seemingly have broader or altered ion transport profiles, also transporting ions such as Zn2+, Ni2+, Cu+, and even Ca2+ (Zielazinski et al., 2012; Raimunda et al., 2012; Moreno et al., 2008; Scherer and Nies, 2009; Seigneurin-Berny et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies showing variable metal specificity.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases appear to have the widest scope of transported ions of the PIB-ATPases.
source: Thus, the PIB-4-ATPases appear to have the widest scope of transported ions of the PIB-ATPases, and it is possible that further subclassification principles and sequence motifs will be identified.
evidence: This is inferred from the discussion of variable metal specificity in the manuscript.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases have been proposed to serve as multifunctional emergency pumps under extreme environmental stress.
source: Due to the broad ion transport range, they have been proposed to serve as multifunctional emergency pumps that can be exploited under extreme environmental stress to maintain heavy-metal homeostasis (Smith et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous speculation.

claim: Available high-resolution structural information of full-length PIB-ATPases is limited to structures of LpCopA and SsZntA.
source: Hitherto, the available high-resolution structural information of full-length PIB-ATPases is limited to two structures each of ion-free conformations of the Cu+-transporting PIB-1-ATPase from Legionella pneumophila (LpCopA) (Gourdon et al., 2011b; Wang et al., 2014), and the Zn2+-transporting PIB-2-ATPase from Shigella sonnei (SsZntA) (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of structural knowledge prior to this study, supported by citations.

claim: The principal architecture of PIB-4-ATPases remains debated.
source: Thus, the principal architecture of the PIB-4-ATPases remains debated, as sequence analyses have proposed different topologies for the N-terminus: with or without (1) the so-called HMBDs, and (2) the first two transmembrane helices, MA and MB (Smith et al., 2014; Andersson et al., 2014; Rosenzweig and Argüello, 2012; Drees et al., 2015), which both are present in other PIB-ATPases (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous conflicting analyses.

claim: sCoaT exhibited clear Zn2+- and Cd2+-dependent ATPase activity.
source: The protein exhibited clear Zn2+- and Cd2+-dependent ATPase activity, while Co2+ only stimulated ATP hydrolysis at high ion concentrations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Co2+ only stimulated sCoaT ATP hydrolysis at high ion concentrations.
source: The protein exhibited clear Zn2+- and Cd2+-dependent ATPase activity, while Co2+ only stimulated ATP hydrolysis at high ion concentrations (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from ATPase assays shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The KM value for Co2+-dependent sCoaT activity measured in this study is higher than previously reported.
source: The fact that the KM value for the Co2+-dependent sCoaT activity reported previously is lower than measured in this study is unexpected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b; Zielazinski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental data to previous studies.

claim: Co2+ and Zn2+ display similar Baginski colour development.
source: However, Co2+ and Zn2+ display similar Baginski colour development as determined by calibration with separate standard curves.
evidence: This is supported by experimental calibration data.

claim: The Malachite Green Phosphate Assay reproduced the relative activity in the presence of Zn2+ and Co2+.
source: However, employment of the alternative Malachite Green Phosphate Assay essentially reproduced the relative activity in the presence of Zn2+ and Co2+, respectively (Lanzetta et al., 1979).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using an alternative assay method.

claim: The relative intracellular availability of Co2+ is more than three orders of magnitude higher than that of Zn2+ in certain bacterial cells.
source: Despite that higher sensitivity has been measured for Zn2+ compared to Co2+, it cannot be excluded that Co2+, rather than Zn2+, is the preferred cargo in vivo as the relative intracellular availability of Co2+ is more than three orders of magnitude higher than that of Zn2+ in certain bacterial cells (Osman et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous measurements of intracellular metal concentrations.

claim: Structures of sCoaT were determined at 3.1 and 3.2 Å resolution.
source: The structures were determined at 3.1 and 3.2 Å resolution, using molecular replacement (MR) as phasing method and SsZntA as search model, and the final models yielded R/Rfree of 24.4/26.8 and 21.8/25.5 (Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data in Table 1.

claim: The two sCoaT crystal forms were obtained using the HiLiDe method.
source: The two crystal forms were obtained using the HiLiDe method (crystallization in the presence of high concentrations of detergent and lipids) (Gourdon et al., 2011a).
evidence: This is a statement about the crystallization method used.

claim: The crystal packing for both sCoaT structures reveal only minor contacts between adjacent membrane-spanning regions.
source: Surprisingly however, the crystal packing for both structures reveal only minor contacts between adjacent membrane-spanning regions, which are critical for the crystals obtained of most other P-type ATPase proteins (Wang et al., 2014; Gourdon et al., 2011b; Sørensen et al., 2006; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of crystal packing shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Type I crystals with unrestrained transmembrane domains have not been reported before for P-type ATPases.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first time that type I crystals with unrestrained transmembrane domains are reported, but a consequence is that peripheral parts of the membrane domain are less well resolved (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the crystal form, with reference to electron density maps.

claim: The PIB-4-ATPase architecture is reminiscent to that of other P-type ATPases.
source: Examination of the structures reveals that the PIB-4-ATPase architecture is reminiscent to that of other P-type ATPases, with three cytosolic domains, A (actuator), N (nucleotide-binding), and P (phosphorylation), as well as a membrane-spanning M-domain (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1a.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases possess eight transmembrane helices: MA, MB, and M1–M6.
source: However, our data unambiguously demonstrate that PIB-4-ATPases possess eight transmembrane helices, MA and MB followed by M1–M6.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing the topology.

claim: MB is kinked by a conserved Gly–Gly motif (G82 and G83) in PIB-4-ATPases.
source: As previously observed for PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases, MB is kinked by a conserved Gly–Gly motif (G82 and G83), forming an amphipathic 'platform', MB', immediately prior to M1, see further below (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by structural data and comparison to other PIB-ATPases.

claim: Many PIB-4-ATPases including sCoaT lack a classical HMBD ferredoxin-like fold.
source: As only the first 47 residues remain unmodelled in the final structures (Table 1), it is clear that many PIB-4-ATPases including sCoaT are lacking a classical HMBD ferredoxin-like fold (typically 70 residues long).
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing insufficient length for a classical HMBD.

claim: The cysteine pair (CGIC) in the N-terminus of sCoaT is positioned in MA, facing M1.
source: In agreement with this observation, the cysteine pair (CGIC in the sequence) in the N-terminus of sCoaT is rather positioned in MA, facing M1 (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 3), in contrast to the surface-exposed, metal-binding CXXC hallmark-motif detected in classical HMBDs.
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 3.

claim: Cysteines in MA are unimportant for sCoaT function.
source: Functional analysis of mutant forms lacking these cysteines in vitro also support that they are unimportant for function (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The sCoaT N-terminus is rich in metal-binding residues (methionine, cysteine, histidine, aspartate, and glutamate).
source: Conversely, the sCoaT N-terminus is rich in metal-binding methionine, cysteine, histidine, aspartate, and glutamate residues, and this feature is conserved among PIB-4-ATPases (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deletion of the first 33 residues of sCoaT has only minor effects on catalytic activity in vitro.
source: We therefore explored the role of this N-terminal tail through assessment of an sCoaT form lacking the first 33 residues. However, in vitro characterization suggests only minor differences compared to wild-type, indicating that the residues upstream of MA are not essential for catalytic activity (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The two obtained sCoaT structures are similar.
source: Surprisingly however, analysis of the two obtained structures suggests that the anticipated significant domain reorientations are absent in sCoaT (Figure 2b), and the models are in contrast rather similar.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Both sCoaT structures are trapped in an E2.Pi like transition state.
source: The compact assembly of the soluble domains and the position of the A-domain near the P-domain, placing the conserved TGE motif responsible for dephosphorylation towards the phosphorylation site, are typically associated with commencement of dephosphorylation, indicating that the two structures are trapped in an E2.Pi like transition state (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a, c, e).
evidence: This is inferred from structural features and comparison to other P-type ATPases.

claim: The E2-BeF3− structure of sCoaT may represent a late E2P state (E2P*).
source: It was proposed that LMCA1 preorganizes for dephosphorylation already in a late E2P state (E2P*, stabilized by BeF3−), in accordance with its rapid dephosphorylation. Favoured occlusion and activation of dephosphorylation directly upon ion release may thus also be the case for sCoaT, and consequently the E2-BeF3− structure captured here may represents a late (or quasi) E2P state (E2P*).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison to LMCA1 and structural features.

claim: The A-domain of sCoaT is rotated towards the P-domain compared to SsZntA.
source: Comparisons of the sCoaT structures to the equivalent structure of SsZntA (E2.Pi) revealed a unique arrangement of the A-domain (Figure 2—figure supplement 4). The TGE-loop region superposes well with the corresponding area in SsZntA, but the rest of the A-domain is rotated towards the P-domain – approximately 14° and 5.3 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The A-domain of sCoaT possesses a surface-exposed extension similar to SERCA.
source: Additionally, we noticed that the A-domain of sCoaT possesses a surface-exposed extension similar to SERCA, but this feature is not present in PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases and it is not a conserved property in the PIB-4 group either (Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and sequence analysis.

claim: The M-domains of the two sCoaT structures appear outward occluded.
source: Conversely, the M-domains of the two sCoaT structures are overall similar and appear outward occluded (Figure 2c), as also supported by comparisons with the equivalent structures of SsZntA, again contrasting to the situation observed in PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases likely employ similar exit pathways lined primarily by M2, M4, M5, and M6.
source: Considering that PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases have overlapping cargo range, share overall topology and that they release ions in free form to the extracellular environment, in contrast to their PIB-1 counterparts, we find it likely that they employ similar exit pathways, lined primarily by M2, M4, M5, and M6 (Figure 2d; Wang et al., 2014; Andersson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison and functional similarities.

claim: The high-affinity-binding site in PIB-4-ATPases is formed by residues from the SPC- and HEGxT-motifs.
source: The high-affinity-binding site in PIB-4-ATPases has previously been suggested to be formed by residues from the conserved SPC- (starting from S325) and HEGxT- (from H657) motifs of M4 and M6, based on X-ray absorption spectroscopy and mutagenesis studies (Zielazinski et al., 2012; Patel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E658 of M6 is pointing away from the ion-binding region around the SPC motif.
source: Among the resides that likely constitute the high-affinity-binding site, remarkably E658 of M6 is pointing away from the ion-binding region around the SPC motif (Figure 2e and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2e and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: E658 rotates away from its ion-binding configuration in the E1P to E2P transition to assist ion release.
source: We anticipate that E658 rotates away from its ion-binding configuration in the E1P to E2P transition, thereby assisting to lower the cargo affinity to permit release via the M2, M4, M5, and M6 cavity (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is inferred from structural data and mechanistic reasoning.

claim: E120 serves as a transient metal ligand, stimulating substrate release.
source: The conserved E120 of M2 (sometimes replaced with an aspartate in PIB-4-ATPases) is located along this exit pathway. The residue also overlays with the conserved E202 in SsZntA (Figure 2f), which has been suggested to serve as a transient metal ligand, stimulating substrate release from the CPC motif of PIB-2-ATPases (Wang et al., 2014). We propose a similar role for E120 in sCoaT as further supported by the decreased activity of E120A sCoaT form (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison and functional data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: H657 serves as an internal counterion in sCoaT.
source: In light of these findings and an earlier report suggesting that a mutation of the equivalent of H657 in MtCtpD leaves the ion affinity unaffected (Patel et al., 2016), we suggest this histidine serves as an internal counterion, similarly as for the invariant lysine in SsZntA, perhaps preventing backtransfer of released ions and for charge stabilization, however we cannot exclude that H657 is also part of the high-affinity-binding site in sCoaT.
evidence: This is inferred from structural data, functional data, and comparison to SsZntA.

claim: H657 is crucial for sCoaT function.
source: Moreover, activity measurements of an alanine substitution of H657 demonstrate that it is crucial for function (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: A conserved K+ site has been suggested to be present in PIB-ATPases.
source: A conserved K+ site, which cross-links between the A- and P-domains in E2 states and thereby allosterically stimulates the E2P to E2 process (Sørensen et al., 2004; Schack et al., 2008), has been suggested to be present also in PIB-ATPases (Sørensen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The A-/P-domain linker in PIB-ATPases is maintained without K+.
source: However, our new E2 structures and available structures of PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases suggest that the A-/P-domain linker is maintained without K+ in PIB-ATPases, and instead is established directly between R273/D601 in sCoaT, as also supported by potassium titration experiments monitoring sCoaT ATPase activity (Figure 3a–d).
evidence: This is supported by structural data and potassium titration experiments shown in Figure 3a–d.

claim: The A-/P-domain point-of-interaction is critical for PIB-ATPases.
source: Nevertheless, the A-/P-domain point-of-interaction appears critical for PIB-ATPases, as functional characterization of R273A, D601A, and D601K result in a marked reduction of turnover (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Substitution of D601 with glutamate suggests that the A-/P-domain distance is critical.
source: Furthermore, substitution of D601 with glutamate suggests that even the A-/P-domain distance is critical (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: KCl leaves the function of sCoaT and SsZntA essentially unaffected.
source: KCl leaves the function of sCoat and SsZntA essentially unaffected in the presence of Zn2+ (cyan) or Cd2+ (grey).
evidence: This is supported by potassium titration data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The P-/A-domain site regulation is K+ independent in PIB-ATPases.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that the P-/A-domain site regulation is K+ independent in PIB-ATPases, in contrast to classical P-type ATPases.
evidence: This is inferred from potassium titration data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases serve as virulence factors in many microbial pathogens.
source: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases serve as virulence factors and are critical for the disease caused by many microbial pathogens, as underscored by the frequent presence of several redundant genes (Sassetti and Rubin, 2003; Joshi et al., 2006; Botella et al., 2011; Pi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Screening of a 20,000-substance library uncovered several compounds that abrogate function of sCoaT and SsZntA.
source: Indeed, screening of a 20,000-substance library using a complementary in vitro assay, uncovers several compounds that abrogate function of sCoaT and SsZntA (Figure 3e, f, data only shown for sCoaT).
evidence: This is supported by inhibitor screening data shown in Figure 3e, f.

claim: Two identified inhibitors have a potent effect against mycobacteria.
source: Furthermore, initial tests of two of these suggest they have a potent effect against mycobacteria, which previously have been shown to be PIB-4 dependent for infection (Patel et al., 2016); 90% of the mycobacteria were killed at mean concentrations of 18.75 and above 50 µM, respectively, using either of these two separate molecules (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is supported by antimycobacterial assay data shown in Figure 3g.

claim: The two inhibitors show considerably less impact on cell survival of primary human macrophages at concentrations up to 25 µM.
source: In contrast, investigation of cytotoxic effects on primary human macrophages at concentrations up to 25 µM demonstrated considerably less impact on cell survival for both blockers (Figure 3h).
evidence: This is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 3h.

claim: The first structure of a PIB-4-type ATPase reveals an eight helix M-domain configuration.
source: Collectively, the first structure of a PIB-4-type ATPase reveals the topology of PIB-4-ATPases, displaying an eight helix M-domain configuration, and likely no HMBDs, at least in members without extended N-termini.
evidence: This is supported by structural data.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases likely have no HMBDs, at least in members without extended N-termini.
source: Collectively, the first structure of a PIB-4-type ATPase reveals the topology of PIB-4-ATPases, displaying an eight helix M-domain configuration, and likely no HMBDs, at least in members without extended N-termini.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing insufficient length for a classical HMBD.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases have an ion-release pathway similar to PIB-2-ATPases.
source: Major findings include the observation of an ion-release pathway similar as in the related PIB-2-ATPases, a previously not observed counterion principle for P-type ATPases, and a unique potassium-independent regulation of the PIB-transport cycle (Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison and supported by Figure 4.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases have a previously not observed counterion principle for P-type ATPases.
source: Major findings include the observation of an ion-release pathway similar as in the related PIB-2-ATPases, a previously not observed counterion principle for P-type ATPases, and a unique potassium-independent regulation of the PIB-transport cycle (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural and functional data showing H657 as internal counterion.

claim: PIB-ATPases have a unique potassium-independent regulation of the transport cycle.
source: Major findings include the observation of an ion-release pathway similar as in the related PIB-2-ATPases, a previously not observed counterion principle for P-type ATPases, and a unique potassium-independent regulation of the PIB-transport cycle (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by potassium titration experiments.

claim: sCoaT was transformed into E. coli C41 strain cells.
source: Forms of the 72 kDa sCoaT from Sulfitobacter sp. NAS14-1 (UniProt ID A3T2G5) were transformed into E. coli (C41 strain) cells.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method.

claim: sCoaT is a 72 kDa protein.
source: Forms of the 72 kDa sCoaT from Sulfitobacter sp. NAS14-1 (UniProt ID A3T2G5) were transformed into E. coli (C41 strain) cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular weight of the protein.

claim: E2-AlF4− crystals were grown with a reservoir solution containing 200 mM MgCl2, 14% PEG1500, and other components.
source: E2-AlF4− crystals were grown with a reservoir solution containing 200 mM MgCl2, 14% (vol/vol) PEG1500, 10 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 3% 2-methyl-2,4-pentanediol, and 100 mM sodium acetate, pH = 5.0.
evidence: This is a description of the crystallization conditions.

claim: E2-BeF3− crystals were grown with a reservoir solution containing 200 mM magnesium formate, 14% PEG5000, and other components.
source: The E2-BeF3− crystals were grown with a reservoir solution containing 200 mM magnesium formate, 14% (vol/vol) PEG5000, 100 mM sodium acetate, pH = 4.0, and 0.5% (vol/vol) 2-propanol was added as an additive.
evidence: This is a description of the crystallization conditions.

claim: Initial phases for the E2-AlF4− structure were obtained by molecular replacement using SsZntA as a search model.
source: For the E2-AlF4− structure, initial phases were obtained by the MR method using software PHASER (McCoy et al., 2007) of the Phenix package (Liebschner et al., 2019), and using the AlF4−-stabilized structure of SsZntA (PDB ID: 4UMW) as a search model.
evidence: This is a description of the structure determination method.

claim: The E2-BeF3− structure was solved using the generated E2-AlF4− structure as a molecular replacement model.
source: The E2-BeF3− structure was solved using the generated E2-AlF4− structure as a MR model.
evidence: This is a description of the structure determination method.

claim: ISOLDE was critical for obtaining the final models with reasonable chemical restraints.
source: ISOLDE (Croll, 2018) in ChimeraX (Goddard et al., 2018) was employed for model building and analysis, and was critical for obtainment of the final models with reasonable chemical restraints and low clash score.
evidence: This is a description of the model building method.

claim: The final sCoaT models are lacking the first 40 residues only.
source: The final models are lacking the first 40 residues only, which is shorter than a classical MBD of 67 amino acids.
evidence: This is a statement about the completeness of the structural models.

claim: The wild-type sCoaT specific activity is 1.00 ± 0.01 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Zn2+ at 50 μM.
source: The wild-type (WT)-specific activity using the employed experimental conditions in the presence of 50 μM metal is 1.00 ± 0.01 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Zn2+ and 2.80 ± 0.06 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Cd2+, comparable to the activity previously measured for PIB-4-ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The wild-type sCoaT specific activity is 2.80 ± 0.06 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Cd2+ at 50 μM.
source: The wild-type (WT)-specific activity using the employed experimental conditions in the presence of 50 μM metal is 1.00 ± 0.01 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Zn2+ and 2.80 ± 0.06 μmol mg−1 min−1 with Cd2+, comparable to the activity previously measured for PIB-4-ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The in vivo transport specificity of CoaT from Synechocystis PCC 6803 can be switched from Co2+ to Zn2+ by exchanging the N-terminal region to that of ZiaA.
source: Interestingly, it has been shown that the in vivo transport specificity of the sCoaT homolog from Synechocystis PCC 6803 (CoaT) can be switched from Co2+ to Zn2+ by exchanging the N-terminal region to that of the Zn2+ transporting PIB-2 ATPase ZiaA from same organism (Borrelly et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: PIB-4-ATPases are able to transport Zn2+ in vivo if the M-domain gains access to the metal.
source: This demonstrates that PIB-4-ATPases not only in vitro (our data), but also in vivo are able to transport Zn2+, if the M-domain gain access to the metal.
evidence: This is inferred from the chimeric construct study and in vitro data.

claim: MB' has been proposed to serve as an interaction site for HMBDs in PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases.
source: Associated, this raises questions also on the role of the above-mentioned MB' platform, which has been proposed to serve as an interaction site for HMBDs in PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases, and for the Cu+-ATPases as a docking site for metal delivering chaperones (Gourdon et al., 2011b; Wang et al., 2014; González-Guerrero and Argüello, 2008; Morin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There are no known zinc/cadmium chaperones for PIB-4-ATPases.
source: As there are no known zinc/cadmium chaperones for PIB-4-ATPases, and because classical HMBDs appear to be missing in at least some proteins of the group, the MB' function may need to be revisited.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge.

claim: The classical view is that the E2P state is outward open and E2.Pi is occluded in P-type ATPases.
source: The classical view of P-type ATPases is that the E2P state is outward open and that the following transition state of dephosphorylation, E2.Pi, is occluded, and that these conformations can be stabilized using the phosphate analogues employed here for structure determination, BeF3− and AlF4−, respectively.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about P-type ATPases.

claim: A narrow exit pathway lined by MA, M2, and M6 remains open in the E2.Pi state for PIB-1-ATPases.
source: Furthermore, distinct ion-release pathways have been proposed among PIB-ATPases (Gourdon et al., 2011b; Wang et al., 2014; Andersson et al., 2014; Mattle et al., 2015), including a narrow exit pathway lined by MA, M2, and M6 that remains open also in the E2.Pi state for the PIB-1-ATPases.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PIB-2-ATPases have a wide opening that becomes reoccluded with the E2P to E2.Pi shift.
source: In contrast, a wide opening extending from the location of the bound metal in the M-domain of ion-occluded states to the non-cytoplasmic side has been observed for the PIB-2-ATPases, and this group becomes reoccluded with the E2P to E2.Pi shift.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The TGE-loop in sCoaT is preorganized for dephosphorylation in the E2P* state.
source: The TGE loop in the E2-BeF3−-stabilized sCoaT (E2P*) is preorganized for dephosphorylation, which is not the case for SsZntA and LpCopA.
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The A-domain rotation in sCoaT may be due to crystal contacts.
source: However, it cannot be excluded that this rotation is due to crystal contacts as the two peripheral β-sheets of the A-domain are interacting tightly with parts of a neighbouring molecule.
evidence: This is speculation based on crystal packing analysis.

claim: Biochemical studies have proposed an ion-binding stoichiometry of one for PIB-4-ATPases.
source: For the PIB-4-ATPases, biochemical studies have proposed an ion-binding stoichiometry of one (Zielazinski et al., 2012; Raimunda et al., 2012; Smith et al., 2017; Patel et al., 2016), however no information is available regarding the presence or absence of counter transport.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: K693 in SsZntA serves as a counterion through interaction with D714 in E2 states.
source: Specifically for the PIB-2-ATPases, a conserved lysine of M5 (K693 in SsZntA) serves as the counterion, through interaction with the conserved metal-binding aspartate of M6 (D714 in SsZntA) in E2 states.
evidence: This is supported by previous structural studies.

claim: PIB-1-ATPases are not Cu+/H+ antiporters.
source: Similarly, PIB-1-ATPases are not Cu+/H+ antiporters, but a likely built-in counterion residue is not conserved in the group (Abeyrathna et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: H657 is sandwiched between S325 and C327 in the E2-BeF3− sCoaT structure.
source: In the E2-BeF3− sCoaT structure, we identify a tight configuration of HEGxT-motif H657, being sandwiched between the SPC residues, distinct from the M5 lysine–M6 aspartate interaction observed in PIB-2-ATPases (Figure 2g, h).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2g, h.

claim: Clear electron density is visible for H657 in the E2-BeF3− structure.
source: Despite the packing issues of the generated crystals, clear electron density is visible for H657, indicating a rigid conformation (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is supported by electron density maps shown in Figure 2g.

claim: A mutation of the equivalent of H657 in MtCtpD leaves the ion affinity unaffected.
source: In light of these findings and an earlier report suggesting that a mutation of the equivalent of H657 in MtCtpD leaves the ion affinity unaffected (Patel et al., 2016), we suggest this histidine serves as an internal counterion, similarly as for the invariant lysine in SsZntA, perhaps preventing backtransfer of released ions and for charge stabilization, however we cannot exclude that H657 is also part of the high-affinity-binding site in sCoaT.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: The interaction between K693 and D714 in SsZntA is only detected in the E2.Pi state.
source: In contrast, for SsZntA the interaction between K693 and D714 is only detected in the E2.Pi state.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of SsZntA structures.

claim: sCoaT preorganizes for dephosphorylation already in the late E2P state.
source: Thus, the interaction pattern is consistent with the idea that sCoaT preorganizes for dephosphorylation already in the (late) E2P state, with the associated occlusion and internal counter–ion interaction taking place earlier than for SsZntA.
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison of sCoaT and SsZntA.

claim: A conserved K+ site cross-links between the A- and P-domains in E2 states in classical P-type ATPases.
source: A conserved K+ site, which cross-links between the A- and P-domains in E2 states and thereby allosterically stimulates the E2P to E2 process (Sørensen et al., 2004; Schack et al., 2008), has been suggested to be present also in PIB-ATPases (Sørensen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The A-/P-domain linker is established directly between R273/D601 in sCoaT.
source: However, our new E2 structures and available structures of PIB-1- and PIB-2-ATPases suggest that the A-/P-domain linker is maintained without K+ in PIB-ATPases, and instead is established directly between R273/D601 in sCoaT, as also supported by potassium titration experiments monitoring sCoaT ATPase activity (Figure 3a–d).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3a–d.

claim: Similar mutations of the K+ site in classical P-type ATPases result in only minor effects.
source: This differs from similar mutations of classical P-type ATPases, where only minor effects are observed (Sørensen et al., 2004; Schack et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PIB-ATPases are more reliant on tight, ion-independent stabilization of the A-/P-domain interaction.
source: It is possible that PIB-ATPases are more reliant on this particularly tight, ion-independent stabilization, as the A–M1/A-domain linker is absent, and because many other P-type ATPases also have a complementary A-/P-domain interaction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is speculation based on structural comparison.

claim: The A-/P-domain regulation is a general feature of many P-type ATPase classes.
source: Thus, our data indicate that this regulation is a general feature of many P-type ATPase classes, yet featuring unique properties for PIB-ATPases.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and functional data.

claim: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases are critical for disease caused by many microbial pathogens.
source: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases serve as virulence factors and are critical for the disease caused by many microbial pathogens, as underscored by the frequent presence of several redundant genes (Sassetti and Rubin, 2003; Joshi et al., 2006; Botella et al., 2011; Pi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PIB-2- and PIB-4-ATPases are missing in humans.
source: In this light and because these P-type ATPases are missing in humans, they represent putative targets for novel antibiotics.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge.

claim: Compounds can be identified that inhibit both PIB-2 and PIB-4 groups.
source: The shared mechanistic principles identified here suggest that compounds can be identified that inhibit both PIB groups, for example directed against the common release pathway, thereby increasing efficacy.
evidence: This is speculation based on the shared mechanistic features.

claim: Mycobacteria have been shown to be PIB-4 dependent for infection.
source: Furthermore, initial tests of two of these suggest they have a potent effect against mycobacteria, which previously have been shown to be PIB-4 dependent for infection (Patel et al., 2016); 90% of the mycobacteria were killed at mean concentrations of 18.75 and above 50 µM, respectively, using either of these two separate molecules (Figure 3g).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: The mean MIC90 value for inhibitor 1 is 18.75 µM against mycobacteria.
source: The mean MIC90 value for inhibitor 1 is 18.75 µM, while for inhibitor 2 it is over 50 µM.
evidence: This is supported by antimycobacterial assay data shown in Figure 3g.

claim: The mean MIC90 value for inhibitor 2 is over 50 µM against mycobacteria.
source: The mean MIC90 value for inhibitor 1 is 18.75 µM, while for inhibitor 2 it is over 50 µM.
evidence: This is supported by antimycobacterial assay data shown in Figure 3g.

claim: Zinc or cadmium release from the high-affinity-binding site is permitted through re-orientation of E658.
source: Zinc or cadmium release from the high-affinity-binding site in the M-domain is likely permitted through re-orientation of E658 (1) in the E1P to E2P transition, thereby lowering the affinity for the occluded ion.
evidence: This is inferred from structural data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: E120 serves as a transient linker between the high-affinity-binding site and the outward environment.
source: E120 serves as a transient linker between the high-affinity-binding site and the outward environment (2).
evidence: This is inferred from structural data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: H657 shifts to a sandwiched position between S325 and C327 following ion release.
source: Following ion-release (3) H657 shifts to a sandwiched position between S325 and C327 (4), acting as a built-in counter ion, preventing backtransfer of the released ion, and allowing completion of the reaction cycle.
evidence: This is inferred from structural data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: H657 acts as a built-in counter ion, preventing backtransfer of the released ion.
source: Following ion-release (3) H657 shifts to a sandwiched position between S325 and C327 (4), acting as a built-in counter ion, preventing backtransfer of the released ion, and allowing completion of the reaction cycle.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and functional data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Atomic coordinates for the sCoaT structures have been deposited at the Protein Data Bank under accession codes 7QBZ and 7QC0.
source: Atomic coordinates and structure factors for the sCoaT AlF4−- and BeF3−-stabilized crystal structures have been deposited at the Protein Data Bank (PDB) under accession codes 7QBZ and 7QC0.
evidence: This is a statement about data deposition.
